claims.claim: TSMC's 2026 demand signal remains unusually strong: January-August consolidated revenue reached NT$3.38687 trillion, up 39.3% year over year, with August revenue up 53.3% year over year.

Management raised full-year 2026 capital spending to US$60-64 billion, with roughly 70-80% allocated to advanced process technology and 10-20% to advanced packaging/testing/mask/other capacity, explicitly tying the increase to structural AI, HPC and agentic-AI demand.

TSMC's Arizona footprint has expanded materially beyond the earlier three-fab framing: its current Arizona site states total planned investment of US$265 billion, including six logic fabs, two advanced-packaging facilities and an R&D center; initial construction of a fourth fab and first advanced-packaging fab began in early 2026.
The next scheduled primary demand checkpoint is September 2026 monthly sales on October 8, 2026; September revenue is not yet published and must remain unknown.

factors.name: AI/HPC demand durability
factors.basis: Primary monthly revenue and Q2 management commentary show strong leading-edge demand and a raised 2026 growth/capex posture.

factors.name: Manufacturing bottleneck power
factors.basis: The capex mix concentrates on advanced process and packaging, reinforcing TSMC's position at multiple constrained layers of AI compute supply.

factors.name: Geographic resilience
factors.basis: Arizona scale adds geographic manufacturing and packaging redundancy, while overseas fabs carry explicit margin dilution and execution complexity.

factors.name: 2nm transition
factors.basis: 2nm already represented 3% of Q2 wafer revenue and is entering a steep ramp, but management expects 3-4 percentage points of gross-margin dilution from the ramp in 2H26.

risks.risk: Management expects the steep 2nm ramp to dilute gross margin by about 3-4 percentage points in 2H26.
Overseas-fab expansion is expected to dilute gross margin by 2-3% in early stages and 3-4% later, creating a real cost of geographic diversification.
Consumer and price-sensitive end markets remain challenged by component prices and macro uncertainty even while AI demand is robust.

causalEdges.mechanism: more accelerator and CPU silicon requires advanced nodes plus packaging capacity
causalEdges.falsifier: AI infrastructure buildout slows materially or customers shift substantial volume away from TSMC-compatible architectures

causalEdges.mechanism: additional US logic and packaging capacity reduces geographic concentration and serves domestic customer requirements
causalEdges.falsifier: cost/yield/timing disadvantages prevent overseas capacity from becoming economically useful

unknowns.unknown: September 2026 revenue is not yet published; the next scheduled release is October 8, 2026.
The exact realized economics and utilization of the expanded US$265 billion Arizona plan remain future execution evidence.

claims.claim: Execution is currently outrunning the prior baseline narrative: Q2 revenue grew 36.0% year over year, net income and diluted EPS grew 77.4%, advanced nodes were 77% of wafer revenue, and management guided Q3 revenue to US$44.6-45.8 billion.
Management raised expected full-year 2026 US-dollar revenue growth to slightly above 40%, supported by very strong AI demand from customers and customers' customers.

Arizona execution has advanced: Fab 1 entered high-volume N4 production in Q4 2024; Fab 2 targets N3 volume production in 2H27; Fab 3 targets N2/A16 by decade-end; Fab 4 and the first advanced-packaging fab entered initial construction stages in early 2026.

factors.name: Execution versus narrative
factors.basis: Revenue, earnings, advanced-node mix and capacity construction provide primary evidence that leading-edge demand is converting into operating results and physical capacity.

factors.name: Expectation burden
factors.basis: Raised growth and capex expectations increase the amount of future utilization, yield and margin execution required to justify the expansion.

factors.name: Margin resilience
factors.basis: Q2 gross margin was 67.7%, but management explicitly forecasts 2nm and overseas-fab dilution during the coming ramp.

factors.name: Capital intensity
factors.basis: US$60-64B of 2026 capex supports future bottleneck capacity but raises execution and return-on-capital requirements.

risks.risk: Security-level valuation attractiveness is not asserted because no canonical live valuation/entry input was part of this work item; this is non-gating.
A high expectation base creates downside sensitivity if AI demand, 2nm yields, packaging throughput or overseas-fab ramps disappoint.
Geopolitical concentration remains material despite geographic expansion because the most advanced capacity and ecosystem cannot be replicated instantly.

causalEdges.mechanism: sustained customer forecasts justify accelerated process and packaging investment
causalEdges.falsifier: future utilization or order visibility falls enough to strand capacity

causalEdges.mechanism: new-node startup and overseas cost structures dilute gross margin before scale efficiencies mature
causalEdges.falsifier: reported margins show no meaningful ramp-related dilution despite the planned capacity profile

contradictions.claim: Exceptional demand and earnings momentum coexist with explicit near-term margin dilution from 2nm and overseas expansion.
contradictions.resolution: Both are supported by the same primary-source management disclosures; strong demand does not eliminate ramp economics.

unknowns.unknown: No canonical security-level valuation or entry recommendation is promoted by this Scout object.
Long-run returns on the expanded Arizona footprint cannot yet be established from current operating history.
